`/home` is the **only writable place in the tree**: project context files cannot be modified by the agent, so it can never rewrite the context that defines its behaviour. `~` is accepted as a shorthand on input (`~/exports/q1.csv`), but the agent always reports the full `/home` path.

## Files users attach to a chat

Users can attach a file to a message with the paperclip in the chat input, by dragging it onto the input, or by pasting it. Accepted formats are `csv`, `tsv`, `txt`, `md`, `json`, `jsonl`, `yaml`, `xml`, `html`, `sql`, `pdf`, `xls`, `xlsx`, `docx` and `parquet`, plus PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP images.

An attachment is uploaded before the message is sent and lands in the sender's own space, under a folder named after the day:

```text
/home/uploads/2026-08-04/sales.csv
```

The agent then treats it like any other saved file: it is listed by `list`, found by `search`, and read by `read`. A second upload of the same name on the same day is suffixed (`sales-2.csv`) rather than replacing the earlier one.

**The agent is only told the path, never the contents.** This is the important part: a 9 MB CSV costs nothing in context until the agent decides to read it, and a large attachment can never push the conversation out of the context window on arrival. The agent reads, greps or queries the file when the question actually needs what is inside.

<Info>
Images are the exception, and are handled the other way round. An image is attached to be *interpreted*, so it is stored with the conversation and sent to the model inline - it is not written to permanent storage, and does not appear in `/home`.
</Info>

Spreadsheets, PDFs, Word documents and Parquet files cannot be read as text. `read` refuses them with an explanation rather than pouring binary into the conversation; the agent parses them with `execute_python` when [Python execution](/nao-agent/chat/capabilities/tools-mcps-skills) is enabled, and otherwise asks for a CSV export.

<Note>
Attaching files needs permanent storage. With `NAO_STORAGE_BACKEND=none` the paperclip only accepts images, and the size limit is the one set by `NAO_STORAGE_MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB`. A message carries at most 5 attachments, and an image at most 5 MB.
</Note>

<Warning>
Viewers cannot upload files, for the same reason they cannot send messages.
</Warning>

## Visualizations and Image Input

The chat UI can render agent query results as charts (bar, line, area, pie, donut, KPI card, scatter, radar, and stacked variants) or as tables with conditional formatting. Both can be edited after the fact, and every chart exposes the SQL query and rows behind it.

For the full list of chart types, the chart edit dialog, table formatting rules, and the project date format setting, see [Visualizations](/nao-agent/chat/capabilities/visualizations).

### Image input

You can attach images directly in the chat input when you want the agent to inspect a screenshot, dashboard, chart, or UI state. The agent treats images as part of the conversation - it can describe them, transcribe text out of them, compare them to data, or use them to disambiguate a question ("the spike in *this* chart").

**How to attach an image**

There are three ways to add images to a message:

- Click the `+` menu in the chat input and pick **Upload image**.
- Drag an image file from your desktop into the chat input - the input shows a highlighted drop zone while you drag.
- Paste an image directly from your clipboard (e.g. after `cmd+shift+4` on macOS or a snipping tool on Windows). The paste handler is scoped to the chat input so pasting elsewhere on the page still works normally.

Selected images appear as thumbnails above the input. Click the small `X` on any thumbnail to remove it before sending.

**Supported formats and limits**

- Formats: `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`.
- Up to **4 images** per message.
- Up to **5 MB** per image.

Files outside these formats or above the size cap are rejected client-side before upload.

**Viewing images in the conversation**

Images you've sent stay attached to the message and re-display when the chat is reloaded or shared. Click any image in the conversation to open it in a full-size lightbox - close it with `Esc`, the X button, or by clicking outside.

Images are stored against your project and served from a stable URL, so they keep rendering inside the chat history and any story or shared link the conversation feeds into.

## Visualizations and file input

The chat UI can render agent query results as charts (bar, line, area, pie, donut, KPI card, scatter, radar, and stacked variants) or as tables with conditional formatting. Both can be edited after the fact, and every chart exposes the SQL query and rows behind it.

For the full list of chart types, the chart edit dialog, table formatting rules, and the project date format setting, see [Visualizations](/nao-agent/chat/capabilities/visualizations).

### Attaching files

You can attach a file to any message, whether it is a screenshot you want the agent to look at or a spreadsheet you want it to work from. There are three ways to do it:

- Click the `+` menu in the chat input and pick **Attach file**.
- Drag a file from your desktop into the chat input - the input shows a highlighted drop zone while you drag.
- Paste from your clipboard (e.g. after `cmd+shift+4` on macOS or a snipping tool on Windows). The paste handler is scoped to the chat input so pasting elsewhere on the page still works normally.

Attachments appear above the input - images as thumbnails, documents as chips showing their name and size - with a small `X` to remove one before sending. A message carries up to **5 attachments**, and anything with an unsupported format or over the size cap is refused with an explanation rather than silently dropped.

**Images** are read by the model directly. Attach one when you want the agent to inspect a dashboard, chart, or UI state: it can describe it, transcribe text out of it, compare it to your data, or use it to disambiguate a question ("the spike in *this* chart"). PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP are accepted, up to 5 MB each.

**Documents** are handled the other way round: they are saved to your [permanent storage](/nao-agent/self-hosting/permanent-storage) under `/home/uploads/<date>/`, and the agent is given the path rather than the contents. It reads, greps or queries the file only when your question needs what is inside, so attaching a large export never eats into the conversation's context. `csv`, `tsv`, `txt`, `md`, `json`, `jsonl`, `yaml`, `yml`, `xml`, `html`, `sql`, `pdf`, `xls`, `xlsx`, `docx` and `parquet` are accepted, up to the instance's upload limit (10 MB by default).

<Note>
Attaching documents needs permanent storage to be enabled on the instance. Where it is turned off, the picker only accepts images.
</Note>

**In the conversation**

Attachments stay with the message and re-display when the chat is reloaded or shared. Click any image to open it in a full-size lightbox - close it with `Esc`, the X button, or by clicking outside. Documents show as chips, with the full storage path in a tooltip, so you can refer the agent back to a file you attached weeks ago.

Images are stored against your project and served from a stable URL, so they keep rendering inside the chat history and any story or shared link the conversation feeds into.

content.text:
Done. Users can now attach documents (`csv`, `xlsx`, `pdf`, `parquet`, and eleven other formats) anywhere they could previously attach an image — same paperclip, same drag-and-drop, same paste — and the two kinds take deliberately opposite routes to the model.

**How the split works.** An image is attached to be looked at, so it keeps its existing path: stored with the conversation in the database and inlined into the request. A document goes to permanent storage instead, under `/home/uploads/<date>/`, and the model is told only its path. That's the whole point of the split — a 9 MB CSV costs nothing in context until the agent decides to read it, and the read goes through the tools it already has (`read`, `list`, `search`, `grep`), so a file attached today is still reachable in a chat next month.

Documents upload through a dedicated multipart endpoint (`POST /api/attachments`) before the message is sent, rather than riding along in the JSON body, which would have hit the body size limit. The chat input shows each one as a chip with a spinner until its path comes back, and refuses to submit while an upload is in flight so a message can never reference a file that isn't there yet.

**One correction to something I'd built earlier in this session.** The system prompt told the agent to parse binary attachments (PDFs, spreadsheets, Parquet) with `execute_python`. That instruction was wrong: `execute_python` builds its virtual filesystem from project-folder text files only, so it cannot see `/home`, and `execute_sandboxed_code` copies in chat images but not stored documents. There is currently no path for the agent to read inside a binary attachment. The prompt now says so plainly and tells the agent to ask for a CSV export instead of guessing from the filename, and both doc pages say the same. Worth knowing as a product gap: binary attachments are storable and findable, but not analysable.

Also finished off the upload route's size handling — it now truncates rather than throwing, so an oversized file produces `sales.csv is larger than the 10 MB upload limit` instead of a bare 413, and the body is drained before any rejection so a refused upload can't leave the request hanging.

**Verification.** Lint, `tsc`, Prettier, and the migration check are all clean. The 113 backend tests and 432 shared tests covering this work pass. Seven pre-existing failures remain in the suite, all environmental and unrelated: a missing `ripgrep` binary, `better-sqlite3` failing to `dlopen`, and two OIDC allowlist tests picking up local `.env` values.

Two things I did not do, both worth a look before this ships: the maintainers handle visual verification per `AGENTS.md`, so the preview strip, document chips, and drop zone are unreviewed; and `docs.json` was already modified before this session, so you may want to confirm the new permanent-storage page is wired into navigation where you want it.
